facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer already sells a system that warns the operator when a machine used in construction, mining or quarrying gets too close to an object.
facts.quote: A manufacturer of heavy off-road machines for construction, mining and quarrying already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer is developing a system that applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react.
facts.quote: It is now developing a system that also applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react.

facts.text: Prototype hardware and software for the heavy off-road machine automatic braking system arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027

facts.text: Validation of the heavy off-road machine automatic braking system must finish in under four months after prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software arrive in mid-2027, and validation must then finish in under four months

facts.text: Past validation of functions comparable to the proposed heavy off-road machine automatic braking system took three to four years of physical testing and per-model tuning.
facts.quote: past validation of comparable functions took three to four years of physical testing and per-model tuning.

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine automatic braking system must work across more than 100 job-site types.
facts.quote: The system must work across more than 100 job-site types

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine automatic braking system must work across more than 10 operating scenarios per machine.
facts.quote: more than 10 operating scenarios per machine

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine automatic braking system must work in rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare.
facts.quote: The system must work across more than 100 job-site types, more than 10 operating scenarios per machine, rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine automatic braking system must work on many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.
facts.quote: and many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.

facts.text: The sensor set for the heavy off-road machine automatic braking system is not fixed, so the research had to cover camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other sensor options.
facts.quote: The sensor set is not fixed, so camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options all had to be covered.

facts.text: The research sought applicable collision-warning and automatic-braking standards and regulations for earth-moving, mining and construction machines in North America, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, South Africa, South America and Asia, including each document's scope, current edition, status, and performance and testing requirements.
facts.quote: in North America, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, South Africa, South America and Asia, and for each, what is the scope, current edition, status, and performance and testing requirement?

facts.text: The research investigated which functional safety requirements apply to a function that can command the brakes on heavy off-road machines.
facts.quote: Which functional safety requirements apply to a function that can command the brakes on these machines?

facts.text: The research investigated whether rules in force or expected by 2028 address safety functions that use machine learning.
facts.quote: Are there rules, in force or expected by 2028, for safety functions that use machine learning?

facts.text: The research investigated what applicable standards and regulations say about test objects, distances, speeds, conditions and pass criteria.
facts.quote: What do these documents say about test methods: test objects, distances, speeds, conditions and pass criteria?

facts.text: The research investigated whether applicable standards and regulations accept simulation or virtual testing as evidence, and under what conditions.
facts.quote: Do any of them accept simulation or virtual testing as evidence, and under what conditions?

facts.text: The research investigated how on-road vehicle regulations and consumer rating programs define acceptance for automatic emergency braking and virtual testing, and which parts could transfer to off-road machines.
facts.quote: How do on-road vehicle regulations and consumer rating programs define acceptance for automatic emergency braking and for virtual testing, and which parts could transfer to off-road machines?

facts.text: The research investigated customer and industry-group requirements that go beyond regulation, including requirements in mining.
facts.quote: Which requirements from customers or industry groups go beyond regulation, for example in mining?

facts.text: The research investigated numeric acceptance measures used in practice—detection rate, false alarms per operating hour, unnecessary brake events and stopping margin—and sought published values where they exist.
facts.quote: Which numeric acceptance measures are used in practice (detection rate, false alarms per operating hour, unnecessary brake events, stopping margin), with published values where they exist?

facts.text: The research ground rules required neutrality toward vendors and technologies.
facts.quote: The ground rules were neutrality toward vendors and technologies

facts.text: The research ground rules required a stated evidence type for every important claim: standard or regulation text, official guidance, vendor claim, or expert opinion.
facts.quote: a stated evidence type for every important claim (standard or regulation text, official guidance, vendor claim, or expert opinion).

facts.text: Each standard and regulation covered by the research was required to carry its edition and date, with drafts and documents under revision flagged as such.
facts.quote: Each standard and regulation was to carry its edition and date, with drafts and documents under revision flagged as such.

facts.text: The research ground rules required rules applying only to on-road vehicles to be marked as on-road-only.
facts.quote: Rules that apply only to on-road vehicles were to be marked

facts.text: The research ground rules prohibited declaring a rule applicable to the heavy off-road machine collision-warning and automatic-braking system unless the source said so.
facts.quote: no rule was to be declared applicable to this system unless the source said so

facts.text: The research ground rules required information not found to be reported as "not found" rather than guessed.
facts.quote: anything not found was to be reported as "not found" rather than guessed.
